answer: Operator Liability Escrow: each agent wallet is cryptographically bound to a named operator, and any cluster of wallets proven to share a controller triggers a graduated escrow seizure against that operator's registered account, scaling with cluster size so the Nth identity costs N times the first. The operator's single wharf of deposited collateral is drained before any wallet is touched. Detection uses a prism of behavioral and funding-graph signals to attribute shared control. Each false identity leaves an ember of liability on the operator, not the wallet.
